rv.q: ...never quite fulfils its potential, offering reflections and textures without cohesion. It all seems to end up working against the play, rather than enhancing it.
Serdar Biliş reaches back over two millennia to adapt Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis and makes it speak, pointedly, uncomfortably, insistently to us, right here, right now.

Turkish director Serdar Biliş brings Euripides’ classic IPHIGENIA to the Arcola in a translation by Stephen Sharkey. With political and military forces exerting a devastating influence over global stability at present, the ancient tale holds an uncomfortably poignant resonance.

cn.t: An earnest but ill-conceived production that struggles with cohesion, jarringly interlacing Euripides' tragedy with contemporary testimonials about male violence in ways that work against rather than enhance the material.
